name: Bloomfield pumping engine
summary: The Boulton & Watt pumping engine set to work at Bloomfield Colliery in 1776, an early working example of Watt's fuel-saving steam engine.
description: Boulton & Watt's single-acting mine-pumping engine at Bloomfield, with a 50-inch cylinder ordered from Wilkinson in June 1775.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.
why: The colliery needed to drain water from its workings, and coal-fired atmospheric engines used a great deal of fuel.

date.label: by 11 March 1776
date.basis: The 11 March 1776 newspaper account, reproduced in an 1868 chronicle, states the engine was set to work on the preceding Friday.

events.statement: Boulton & Watt's single-acting mine-pumping engine at Bloomfield, with a 50-inch cylinder ordered from Wilkinson in June 1775.
events.caveats: The original Gazette issue and original cylinder order were not independently inspected; the 1868 newspaper transcription was inspected. This does not establish a first commercial offer or universal priority.

50-inch Wilkinson cylinder ordered June 1775 and engine set to work March 1776.

community_entry.community: Owners and workers at Bloomfield Colliery
community_entry.rationale: A named mine operating a full-sized engine is direct deployment beyond earlier workshop trials.
community_entry.caveats: The Gazette issue was inspected through an 1868 transcription; the date is a latest bound and does not establish first commercial availability.

caveats: The cited newspaper and original order were not separately retrieved. This is not claimed to be the first steam engine or the origin of every later engine.

links.statement: Wilkinson's large-cylinder machining supplied Bloomfield's 50-inch cylinder; the technical history associates this scale of supply with his stationary-cylinder through-bar arrangement.
links.scope: Bersham manufacture for Bloomfield, order June 1775 and operation March 1776.
links.alternatives: Other founders supplied other castings, and different boring-machine designs existed.
links.caveats: Exact machine commissioning and machining record for this individual cylinder were not inspected; the supplier is firmer than the reconstructed configuration-to-product assignment.
links.timing: Production occurs in the 1775–76 supply interval and before engine operation; overlapping intervals reflect uncertain machine dating, not a later cause.

evidence.supports: Named 50-inch supply and historical reconstruction of the large-cylinder boring method.
Bersham boring works and Wilkinson's sustained cylinder-supply role.

links.statement: The successful Soho development work was followed by the partners supplying a full-size commercial pumping engine at Bloomfield.
links.scope: Boulton & Watt development and supply programme, Soho to Tipton, 1775–1776.
links.alternatives: Patent extension, commercial organization, site erection and another Wilkinson cylinder also mattered.
links.caveats: Bloomfield was a newly built installation, not the same experimental engine moved to a mine.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 15, consecutive trial and Bloomfield paragraphs
evidence.supports: Explicit transition from promising trials to customer engines and Bloomfield operation.
